correctness.rationale: For fixed odd n≥5 and a fixed first angle, the n−1 independent area differences have derivative given by c_n times the step-two cyclic difference, followed by subtraction of the last component. In its kernel the cyclic differences are constant and hence sum to zero; step two generates the odd cycle and u_0=0 then forces every correction to vanish. The determinant constraints are jointly C¹ in the angles/mark and the C² radial parameter. The shared circular derivative and compactness of the marked-angle circle give uniform local uniqueness and existence radii (equivalently use the common inverse and a uniform contraction on a small correction ball). Small C² distance gives positive radial curvature and preserves the ordering and positivity of the signed doubled areas. Normalizing a fixed ellipse to the circle gives a nearby radial graph via the angular projection; a reflecting affine map requires reversing cyclic order if a positive sign is wanted, without changing the marked point or area equality. Differentiating the three radial products gives the stated G_j, and the common derivative is its average. For even n≥6 the alternating functional kills the angular derivative and evaluates to −2n sin(2Δ) on the stated mode, so excludes differentiable continuation through these prescribed regular angles only.
residual_risks: The radii are existential and depend on fixed n; no assertion concerning global uniqueness or even-order existence was checked or made.

value.rationale: This resolves a local, all-marked-points version of a published exact inscription question on genuinely nonconic ovals. Uniqueness and the inverse deformation equation distinguish persistence from approximation or classification, and the even-order mode gives a concrete limit of differentiable continuation rather than a claim of global nonexistence.
residual_risks: Not a global solution for general convex curves or a quantitative neighborhood bound.
